# PDF fixture licenses

Each fixture under `tests/fixtures/pdfs/` is recorded here with its provenance
and license. Fixtures land in phase 2 (`digital-clean/*.pdf`), phase 3
(`digital-broken/*.pdf`), phase 4 (`image-scan/*.pdf`), and phase 9 (full
benchmark corpus including `mixed/` and `edge/`).

| Fixture | Phase added | Source | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-2col.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). ASCII content, two pages. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-en-mixed.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). ASCII content mixing two paragraphs. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-table.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). One page with a 3-by-3 grid table. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-clean/lorem-ar-real.pdf` | 2 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + a system Noto / DejaVu Arabic-capable TTF). One page carrying real Arabic codepoints in the text layer. The visual rendering is not bidi-shaped because we deliberately avoid pulling in `arabic_reshaper` / `python-bidi` (their licenses do not match the project's allow-list) — the test layer's job is to exercise Unicode plumbing, not to be visually correct. Phase 9 enriches the corpus with bidi-shaped Arabic. | MIT (project-owned generated artefact; embedded font remains under the system font's own license — Noto OFL or DejaVu Bitstream Vera; both permit subset embedding by `reportlab`). |
| `digital-broken/mojibake.pdf` | 3 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). Synthetic broken-text-layer fixture: short single- and two-character `?`-style tokens that diverge sharply from the Arabic word-length reference distribution. Exercises the validator's word-boundary KL signal. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-broken/replacement-glyphs.pdf` | 3 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Helvetica). Synthetic broken-text-layer fixture: text layer dominated by U+25A0 BLACK SQUARE plus PUA codepoints — the failure mode of glyph-id-not-Unicode encodings. Exercises the validator's replacement-glyph signal. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `digital-broken/broken-glyph-id-layer.pdf` | bugfix-14 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` via direct PDF content-stream construction (reportlab silently rewrites raw control bytes to U+25A0). Synthetic broken-text-layer fixture mimicking the Foulabook failure mode: text layer carries font-specific glyph identifiers in the ASCII control range (\\x01..\\x1F) plus bogus Latin runs, with no real Arabic codepoints. Exercises the bugfix-14 extension to the replacement-glyph signal that counts ASCII control codepoints (excluding `\\t\\n\\v\\f\\r`) as replacement glyphs. | MIT (project-owned) |
| `image-scan/scan-ar-1col.pdf` | 4 | Generated by `tools/generate_fixtures.py` (reportlab + Pillow). One-page synthetic image-scan: a Pillow-rendered raster (title + three paragraph lines) embedded as the only content of a PDF page. Zero text layer — phase 3's validator rejects, phase 4's layout detector takes over. Pillow draws using its built-in default font; no system-font dependency. Phase 9 will replace this with real scanned-Arabic provenance. | MIT (project-owned generated artefact). |

## Phase 9 additions

### Reference snapshots

Phase 9 added sibling reference files for the e2e acceptance tests
in `tests/test_e2e.py`. Each `<fixture>.expected.md` captures the
byte-identical Markdown snapshot the native path is expected to
produce; regenerate only when the upstream emitter contract changes
intentionally (and a PR explains the change).

| Reference | Source | License |
|---|---|---|
| `digital-clean/*.expected.md` | Generated by running the native pipeline against the sibling `*.pdf` and capturing the emitter's output. Regeneration: `python -m arabic_pdf_transcribe.cli FIXTURE.pdf -o FIXTURE.expected.md --quiet`. | MIT (project-owned generated artefact) |

### Scope and follow-ups

Phase 9 deliberately keeps the corpus focused on synthetic,
reproducibility-focused fixtures rather than chasing real Arabic
PDFs of uncertain provenance. Real-corpus expansion (InDesign /
LaTeX-bidi / Wikisource) and the threshold-tuning carry-over from
phase 3's review (`min_arabic_ratio`, presentation-form handling)
are post-v1 follow-ups so they land together with the data they
depend on. ML-path CER reference texts for the `image-scan` and
`mixed` fixtures are also part of that follow-up.

The license-audit harness is permissive about fixture content (it
reads only `models.toml` and the live distribution set) — fixture
licensing is enforced manually at PR-review time, not in CI.
